Here's Arch Linux page on streaming media. I think they're all lightweight until you want to transcode. I'm sure Ubuntu has most of them in their repos, although configuration may differ. I remember MediaTomb being pretty easy to set up.

I'd try Plex. It's insanely easy to set up (it's all graphical), lightweight, and feature complete imo. The stuff you get with the premium version are just niceties, actual functionality is all there in the free version. Install it, add your user to the plex group, plex to your user group, and be sure to take full ownership+rwx rights to all your media and you're golden. Idk what your specs are but I'm willing to bet Plex would run smoothly for you as long as you have 1 gig of ram +2.0 single core/1.5 dual core cpu or better.

Look into minidlna. It's not actually a streaming server; it's more of a traditional file server, but using the dlna protocol that all the modern network media players seem to expect. I started using it when I switched my primary htpc from XBMC to an actual Xbone because the media player doesn't support nfs or anything else reasonable. It has some drawbacks that you'll quickly discover, but it's very lightweight, and it puts all of the streaming work on the client, so your laptop won't burst into flames.
You can always give emby a shot. It's a media server started by some ex-kodi devs. Tons of features and apps for a whole slew of devices.
